stories.title: Unregistered hydrogen inhalers flooding Malaysia market, expert cautions against use
stories.summary: Unregistered hydrogen inhalers claiming to treat chronic diseases are widely sold in Malaysia, costing RM7,000 to RM8,000, with some sellers making unverified health claims. Experts warn these devices lack proven benefits and safety data, with potential risks from harmful by-products if poorly made. The Health Ministry states hydrogen inhalers are unapproved by authorities, and selling unregistered devices is illegal and potentially dangerous. PETALING JAYA, Selangor – From eye spas to lung detox treatments, unregistered hydrogen inhalers are flooding the market in Malaysia, with some making bold claims of easing chronic diseases. While most sellers caution that these inhalers are not a replacement for medical treatment, some have made unverified claims that they can help patients with cataracts, diabetes, thyroid disorders, asthma and even cancer. These machines allow users to inhale hydrogen gas, which is purported to cleanse the lungs, while some also come with special eye goggles claimed to help alleviate eye-related ailments. They are also said to produce hydrogen-rich drinking water. Checks on online platforms and with sellers showed that the machines are being sold for between RM7,000 (S$2,200) and RM8,000, with some offering instalment plans. Some sellers have also resorted to organising roadshows where participants can try the machines for a small fee, ranging from RM29 to RM59 per session. The Star approached a seller who claimed that daily use of the machine could “refresh” the body. “Most of my clients are seniors, and I offer instalments for those who cannot fork out RM7,000 in one go to help ease their or their children’s financial burdens,” he said. When asked about its benefits, the seller claimed that the machine could provide almost instant results.

stories.title: Ukraine has only 72% of minimum gas volume required for winter by end of summer
stories.summary: MOSCOW, August 23. Ukraine has accumulated only about 9.6 billion cubic meters (bcm) of gas in the underground storages by the end of August, which is 72% of the minimum volume of 13.2 billion cubic meters required to get through the winter, TASS calculations show. Ukraine had previously virtually abandoned gas imports from Europe due to high prices and is filling its storages only with its own production, but these volumes will not be enough to prepare for the winter. If the current rates are maintained, Ukraine will be able to pump an additional 2.2-2.5 bcm into the storages by November 1; the total volume will amount to no more than 12.1 bcm. Ukraine planned to boost the gas reserves to 14.6 bcm by winter.
